approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only scores accepted in the current session. It keeps the best sixty-four molecules and samples parents from their upper score bands. A proposal either recombines connected fragments of two parents, sometimes followed by a mutation, or makes one to three successive atom, bond or ring edits to one parent. Canonical identity checks, duplicate rejection and a source-relative sulfur rule admit a fresh pool of 160 offspring. A Gaussian process fitted to count-valued Morgan fingerprints ranks this pool through correlated posterior draws, choosing ten distinct molecules for evaluation. After three batches without an incumbent improvement, only the forty highest posterior means are eligible until progress resumes. Accepted scores update both the full fitting archive and the breeding population. The Parent contains no corpus-derived fragment relation and no operator that swaps a connected internal core while deliberately preserving both surrounding molecular fragments.
approach.novelty: Add one context-matched internal-core exchange at the existing insertion primitive. When that primitive is selected, two eligible cuts identify a small connected middle and two exterior fragments. An unlabeled corpus relation supplies a different middle compatible with both local attachment environments; the constructor preserves both exteriors and certifies the two new joins. If there is no eligible support, the original insertion runs. This differs from the earlier failed one-cut graft, which replaced the whole mutation menu and preserved only one exterior, and from coarse motifs selected without attachment-context matching. Same-Parent siblings changed prediction, allocation, search control or removed existing routes; they did not add this two-sided construction. The hypothesis is that preserving the two existing exterior relationships makes some internal replacements useful to subsequent search. More scaffolds or larger edits by themselves do not support it.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is weak conversion of proposed structural alternatives into sustained useful accepted progress. The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has complete mean 0.607030316211131 and population SD 0.030175277546149237. Its three original summary.json and run.log files confirm complete successful Search execution. A fresh read of all fifteen Parent trajectories and session logs gives 435 full pools, 4350 paid optimizer records with 4350 observed-feedback joins, 634 strict best-generating-parent wins and positive margin mass 16.891241376231875, 253 sequential incumbent wins and mass 5.978073077532332. Only 1.0224077547621127 of that incumbent mass occurs at optimizer ordinals 146..290 (2175 records), and 88 pools use the stall mask. These are the current Parent measurements, not numbers borrowed from its mask-free predecessor. The source offers local insertion and other atom/bond edits plus crossover, but no deliberate two-flank core exchange. This missing capability is a testable candidate explanation, not an established cause. The prior n-9f11b684e560 one-cut recipe delivered 2867 changed paid graft products, 2770 next-fit joins and 1571 later breeders; its parent-margin mass nevertheless fell 17.25153528627184 to 15.276942412130648 and its endpoint fell -0.0442135983776937 against its own code Parent n-1744a1494180. Keep its canonical mechanism_result=confirmed and falsifier_status=triggered together. n-814ee0b4f000 delivered 746 coarse-motif purchases but lost -0.05337593156335637; n-e1a97c9e8713 broadened breeding diversity yet lost -0.047212619373212715. Those are contrary evidence against edit size or variety alone. n-060debe936b2 removed the present Parent crossover route and lost -0.051489597325333016, so the present ticket preserves that route. Evidence: each cited node's nodes/<node_id>/analysis.json, molecular.json and optimize.py; the source files and exact hashes read here are enumerated in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and its fifteen audit-seed-<Search seed>-<issued task>.json files, with their underlying run-relative trajectory, log, summary and run-log inputs. Historical narrative recommendations are not treated as capabilities or causal findings.

method_change.previous_method: Actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de uses its inherited seven-primitive atom/bond/ring mutation menu; insert_atom splits one selected bond by one sampled atom.
method_change.proposed_method: At that unchanged insertion draw, perform a supported, certified two-attachment internal-core exchange; use the exact original insertion when the fixed relation has no eligible support.
method_change.rationale: The actual Parent shows diminishing late incumbent gain. Prior one-cut grafts and untargeted coarse motifs were purchased but did not improve their endpoints; they did not preserve two exterior relationships simultaneously. The pinned full CReM permutation helper supplies this missing construction capability without changing the rest of the current Parent search.

hypothesis: Modify only the insert_atom construction boundary of n-cf8d309c06de. The unchanged seven-primitive dispatcher still chooses insert_atom with weight 0.12 on each existing inner attempt, including ordinary continuation and optional crossover finishing. At that call, enumerate every unordered pair of eligible heavy-atom non-ring SINGLE bonds, provided the substrate has at most 30 such bonds. Remove both edges and retain exactly three connected components: one nonempty connected middle incident to both cuts and two nonempty exterior components each incident to one cut. The runtime middle has 1..10 heavy atoms. Construct its two labeled attachment/context fragments and obtain the full pinned CReM radius-three nonstereo context/core permutation set. Query a newly prepared relation for incoming connected two-attachment cores of 1..12 heavy atoms and size difference -2..+2; exclude every mapped-core identity in the current middle's full permutation set. A distinct core means a distinct canonical nonstereo atom-map-labeled graph, so automorphic duplicates count once, while two inequivalent boundary assignments of an asymmetric core remain separate alternatives. Uniformly choose one supported physical cut pair and then one distinct compatible mapped-core row using the existing session Python RNG. Preserve both complete exterior atom/bond subgraphs, remove only the middle and its two cut edges, and join each exterior endpoint to its corresponding incoming attachment neighbor by one SINGLE bond. There is one assembly per selected row and no lookahead product ranking or frequency weighting. If the substrate exceeds the cut limit, has no structurally eligible pair, or has no distinct compatible support, consume no constructor RNG and execute the original insert_atom body. An eligible selected construction is not replaced by original insertion merely because its later inherited sanitation, size, sulfur or duplicate check fails. The existing bounded caller handles ordinary invalid products. Mapping, table-integrity and preservation-certificate failures are explicit technical errors. The intended path is new certified two-sided core changes, paid exposure and real feedback/reuse, then potentially greater incumbent progress and final Top-1. Immediate exterior preservation is not a promise that later mutation or descendant construction leaves those exteriors intact.

finding_summary.headline: Two-exterior core swaps reached feedback, but useful progress shrank and the endpoint fell by 0.0504
finding_summary.insights:
Both borrowed CReM elements operated: the unlabeled relation supplied compatible cores, and the full equivalent-attachment assignment helper supported mapped construction with two preserved exterior fragments. This settles the registered insertion-only variant: correct two-sided preservation and real downstream exposure were insufficient to deliver the required endpoint benefit. It leaves the broader constructive-fragment approach open and does not revise the earlier one-cut result. The experiment jointly tests this relation, mapping, uniform draw and insertion placement; it does not identify which element caused the loss or assess full upstream CReM.

The search still concentrates useful evaluations in narrow families. The five high-score groups occupy only 10, 9, 29, 23 and 18 typed scaffolds, despite 1,501 typed scaffolds across all accepted outputs. Of 4,350 purchases, 1,603 were bred entirely from molecules accepted in the immediately preceding batch, and the oldest generating parent averaged 2.88 batches old. In the late half, 57 purchases belonged to a same-session exact-score group with at least five late members, fewer than the Parent's 114. Mean within-batch correlation between predicted and realized ranks on the ten purchased molecules was 0.528, versus 0.515 for the Parent. Those selected-stream measurements do not diagnose how the surrogate ranks the unpurchased alternatives. The family concentration supports a continuing limitation in generating and sustaining useful alternative core/linker families; reduced late ties do not explain the endpoint regression. A score-conditioned core proposal operator or a search scheme capable of developing distinct functional arrangements could address that limitation; this result does not validate either method or a generic diversity reward.

The Molecular assessment also shows why graph preservation is a limited chemistry guarantee. Median size increased from 28 to 30 heavy atoms, while molecules above fifty heavy atoms rose from 44 to 194; the small tail remained, with 99 molecules below six atoms versus 91. Typed/generic scaffold counts fell from 1,667/951 to 1,501/941. Reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unassigned stereocentres remain common, and no specified retained stereochemistry was exposed in the formal construction records. The immediate certificates establish connectivity and recorded attribute correspondence. They establish neither retained structure after later edits nor synthetic feasibility, and the chemical flags are descriptive associations rather than demonstrated causes of the score loss.
finding_summary.results:
The construction was exposed to real feedback. Across 15 Search sessions, 9,283 insertion opportunities produced 7,308 checked immediate core replacements with passing two-exterior certificates; 7,307 changed molecular identity. 6,525 final pool members carried such a replacement and 254 were purchased in 15 sessions. Of those purchases, 229 still had a certified immediate identity and 25 had undergone further ordinary continuation. All 249 nonterminal purchases entered the next fit; 5 final-batch purchases had no next-fit opportunity. 207 entered the survivor population and 141 were actually used in later breeding. No recorded attachment-support, row-membership, exterior-map or checked-certificate discrepancy was found.

The endpoint benefit did not follow. Across all 4,350 purchases, strict wins over the original generating parent(s) increased to 677 from 634, but their total positive margin was 15.957361, compared with 16.891241 for the Parent. Sequential incumbent gain was 5.221986 versus 5.978073; over the last 145 purchases per session it was 0.922456 versus 1.022408. Late positive parent margin did rise slightly, to 4.519276 from 4.402370. The complete macro mean fell from 0.607030316 to 0.556624514, a paired change of -0.050405802 against the registered +0.002 requirement. All three seed macro scores fell; five task/seed endpoints improved and ten declined. The fixed productive-neighborhood prediction is therefore refuted after successful construction and feedback activation. This was a complete execution, with no missing score cells or budget failures.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatics and bridged amines retain reactive halogen motifs, undefined stereochemistry, and both size extremes
molecular.overall_character: This assessment describes n-06e791e9d199 against the actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de on frozen Search seeds 0/1/2. The request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent task trajectories were read; no task or paired trajectory is missing. Each contains 300 accepted observations, including ten initial molecules. Descriptor denominators below exclude those initial records: 870 optimizer molecules per task and 4350 per node. These are accepted outputs, not every unpurchased pool member or rejected suggestion. The Child outputs are predominantly ring-containing and aromatic: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9724-0.9793 and aromatic-text rates 0.9529-0.9782. They range from indole/benzimidazole carboxamides through linked aza aromatics and carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles to densely bridged tertiary amines. Median heavy-atom count is 30 versus 28 for Parent; the Child still has 99 molecules below six heavy atoms and 126 below twelve, while 194 exceed fifty, compared with Parent counts 91, 124 and 44 under identical strict inequalities. The largest Child graph has 119 heavy atoms. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko identities number 1501/941 for Child and 1667/951 for Parent; empty scaffolds account for 106/95 molecules separately. Broad connectivity variation therefore coexists with narrow high-score families, rather than global scaffold collapse. The chemistry is not uniformly makeable: N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, aminooxy groups, imines, small fused rings, and congested cages recur alongside ordinary amides and heterocycles. No synthetic route, stability, protonation or conformational feasibility was established. The Child does show formal charge in 230 molecules and carbon bearing multiple halogens in 260, versus 0 and 24 for Parent by the same definitions; neither capability is absent. No specified tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemistry was observed. RDKit-perceived SP3 stereocentres remain unassigned in 2018 Child molecules; non-SP3 perception hits were excluded from that count. All numeric chemistry readings were derived from the supplied trajectories using RDKit 2023.09.6; motif SMARTS, strict size tails, scaffold and stereo definitions, individual input filenames and SHA256 hashes are in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files. The Child files are the actual trusted slot-1 staging inputs named by the immutable request; its node archive did not exist when read. The Parent inputs are its published Search archive files. No future Child archive is claimed as evidence. Score gradients below are associations within dependent observed streams, not proof that a chemical motif caused a score change or that any construction component produced it.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted optimizer molecules have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1-42, and median three perceived rings. The high-score family is compact, largely aromatic indole/benzimidazole-like carboxanilide chemistry with methyl, methoxy, haloaryl and amide-N substituents. The best observed molecule is a 24-heavy-atom, four-ring N-methyl anilide bearing an annulated N-formyl ring; its ring basis includes a four-membered ring. The 25-heavy-atom benzimidazole-like leaders instead carry amide-N halomethyl substituents. These retain recognizable medicinal functional groups, but the fused small ring and reactive substituent variants prevent a blanket synthetic-plausibility claim. The Parent also concentrates on similarly sized aromatic carboxamides: both high-score deciles have median 25 heavy atoms. The Child is not lacking rings or amides.
liabilities: Nitrogen-halogen bonds occur in 288 optimizer molecules, including 31 of the high-score 87; the same counts for Parent are 404 and 86. Their presence is a chemical liability even where an observed score is favorable.
The best molecule contains a fused four-membered N-containing ring. That topology requires a specific feasibility assessment; RDKit sanitation supplies no synthesis certificate.
Nineteen molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms, including scored-zero fragments. These cannot retain the multi-ring/carboxamide arrangement associated with the high-score family.
missing_features: High-scoring scaffold alternatives remain limited: the top 87 occupy ten nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds, against 197 over the whole stream. The observed useful aromatic/carboxamide arrangement is explored mainly through close analogues rather than many independent core arrangements.

Stable peripheral chemistry is not consistently retained alongside that useful core: high-score carboxamides coexist with N-halogen and N-halomethyl variants. The trajectory shows the association with the core, not evidence that those reactive substitutions are necessary.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole fluoroanilide scores 0.3051048083696145, whereas the N-formyl annulated carboxanilide reaches 0.4811252243246881. All 87 molecules in the Child high-score decile retain a carbonyl-amide/lactam motif, and their heavy-atom range is 23-26. By contrast, ethene, peroxide and halogen-only fragments have score 0.0. Several benzimidazole carboxamides differing only by amide-N chloromethyl, fluoromethyl or bromomethyl score exactly 0.47189631731668286. Thus preserving a compact aromatic/carbonyl framework separates leaders from destructive fragmentation; swapping halogen identity within that particular framework does not show a reward gradient. This comparison does not identify an unseen target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most chemically uneven stream: median 38 heavy atoms, range 1-119, with 163 molecules above fifty heavy atoms versus eighteen in Parent. High scorers instead have 29-41 heavy atoms and typically three aza-aromatic rings. The leading 34-heavy-atom molecule joins a butyl/ethyl-substituted bipyridyl region to another pyridyl ring through an NH-CH(F) linkage, with an N-chlorinated aminooxy substituent and an O-Br bond. Another trajectory reaches positively charged N=O and iminium-like substituents on thioether-linked aza aromatics. The seed-0 leader is a much larger 72-heavy-atom, nine-ring imine/hydrazone-rich structure. The Parent leaders include more compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl/thione systems and nitrile-bearing aromatic families; those Parent structures also carry reactive or strained motifs and are not synthetic controls.
liabilities: There are 242 O-halogen and 288 N-halogen-containing molecules. The leading aminooxy/N-chloro and aryl-O-Br combination is a substantial synthetic and stability concern.
Formal charge appears in 228 molecules, including unusual N=O/iminium patterns. These are not evidence of controlled medicinal protonation-state exploration.
Long imine/hydrazone networks and extensive graph growth occur alongside sixteen molecules below six heavy atoms. Both extremes remain visible; neither is hidden by the compact leaders.
missing_features: Compact presentation of several heteroaryl environments is not maintained across sessions: the very large imine/hydrazone family lacks the size discipline shown by the better observed linked-ring family. This is a within-output contrast, not a claim that molecular size alone determines the objective.

Stable acceptor-bearing alternatives are unevenly represented. Only four Child molecules contain a nitrile, compared with 257 Parent molecules, including 31 in the Parent high-score decile. That is a coverage difference, not proof that nitrile installation would raise a score.
The best NH-CH(F)-aryl linker has an unspecified tetrahedral configuration; a defined spatial arrangement of its substituents is missing even though the molecular graph is accepted.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading linked aza-aromatic molecule scores 0.6409375933114363, while the heavily expanded methoxy/imine-rich low example scores 0.3236331203849664. Tiny fragments such as the chlorinated alkoxide-alkyne and difluorine score 0.5, so that baseline does not establish useful chemistry. The Child high-score decile is smaller than the full stream and has no molecule above fifty heavy atoms; sheer graph expansion is not rewarded in these observed leaders. Yet 61 of the high-score 87 retain O-halogen bonds, and the final charged aza-aromatic example scores 0.6204859047996303. The visible scoring association tolerates conspicuously reactive decoration and should not be read as a stability preference.

per_task.generated_character: The stream has median 32 heavy atoms, range 1-92, and median six perceived rings. Its best 23-heavy-atom structure is a chlorinated, densely bridged tertiary-amine cage attached through an azetidine unit to a pyrrole; RDKit perceives eight rings and six unassigned SP3 stereocentres, including a bridge nitrogen. Nearby leaders exchange halogen, bridge and small-ring connectivity. Other seeds produce less compact fused aromatic/amine systems, so the whole stream is not one cage. Parent high scorers have a similar size range but fewer rings: high-decile medians are 27 heavy atoms and three rings for Parent versus 26 and six for Child. Ring nitrogens and potentially basic amines are abundant rather than missing.
liabilities: Forty-nine of the high-score 87 contain a ring of four atoms or fewer, versus eight in Parent. Small rings can be viable, but dense bridges and multiple fusions require geometric scrutiny rather than treating valence validity as feasibility.
The full stream includes 97 O-halogen-containing molecules, eighteen below six heavy atoms and 21 above fifty heavy atoms. The favorable cage examples do not characterize those tails.
missing_features: Defined configuration is missing at the very centres that control cage and linker geometry: 86 of the high-score 87 have unassigned SP3 stereocentres and none has specified tetrahedral stereo.

Less strained ways to present the observed amine/aromatic relationship are underrepresented among the Child leaders relative to the Parent high-score family. The output alone cannot establish that the highly bridged conformations are physically accessible.
All molecules are formally neutral despite the many amine centres. Their relevant protonation states and pKa values have not been established by these SMILES or scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged amine/pyrrole leader scores 0.9952400440331282, whereas the N-chloro carboxamide of an arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine scores 0.00016650955053713697 and a small fluoroether scores 0.002873534464898831. Every high-decile molecule matches the neutral nonaromatic nonamide nitrogen query, while none retains a sulfonamide or carboxylic acid; those groups are frequent in the low-score set. The association supports aromatic surfaces together with accessible amine environments in this stream, not a causal rule about any isolated group. A later cage-linked expansion scores only 0.6755340103112975, so more ring connectivity is not uniformly rewarded. Parent also reaches high scores with less heavily bridged amino-ring frameworks; the Child cage is not the only observed productive shape.

per_task.generated_character: The stream has median 31 heavy atoms, range 1-62, and median five perceived rings. Its leaders combine propyl/ethoxy-substituted aryl groups with [nH]-bearing, N-methylated carbonyl heterocycles and additional benzene fusion. The best 31-heavy-atom molecule has four perceived rings, including a nine-membered ring; it should not be described simply as an ordinary small fused bicyclic scaffold. Other seeds retain larger bridged lactam/amine or annulated dione arrangements. Familiar ether, lactam and aromatic groups coexist with nonstandard ring topology. Parent leaders more often retain saturated amine/lactam arrangements rather than the Child high-score set's extensively conjugated dione systems.
liabilities: Fifty-one molecules contain a perceived ring of four atoms or fewer whose atoms are all aromatic, versus eighteen in Parent. This is a graph-level strain/planarity flag, not a proof of geometric impossibility.

The stream includes 35 N-halogen, fifteen O-halogen and 25 O-O-single-bond-containing molecules. These unnecessary-looking reactive variants remain possible around the otherwise recognizable lactam/ether chemistry.
Twenty-two molecules fall below six heavy atoms and eight exceed fifty, compared with eleven and four in Parent. Neither size extreme is represented in the high-score decile.
missing_features: The high-score family lacks broad alternatives to its particular aryl-to-conjugated-dione connection. The Parent shows other carbonyl/amine ring arrangements at comparable size; this is evidence of a coverage gap rather than a prescription for an unseen target structure.

Chemically straightforward ring organization is inconsistent: enlarged heteroaromatic rings, additional fusion and bridge changes can preserve the score motif without establishing accessible geometry or a practical synthesis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial heterocyclic dione aryl ester scores 0.1678386594791329 and the propyl/ethoxy aryl fused-dione leader reaches 0.22950021766420825. All high-score 87 retain a carbonyl amide/lactam environment and have 29-34 heavy atoms. Atomic or two-atom fragments score 0.0. A late N-chloro lactam analogue remains below the leader at 0.20548046676563256. The observable gradient favors retaining a substantial aryl/carbonyl-heterocycle arrangement over fragmentation, but nearby expanded ring variants differ only modestly and no unique missing target fragment can be inferred. The Parent high-score set contains 42 typed nonempty scaffolds versus 23 for Child, so chemical connectivity coverage is narrower near the Child leaders despite 452 typed scaffolds over its full stream.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer molecules have median 28 heavy atoms, range 1-52, and median four perceived rings. The best 27-heavy-atom structure combines a fused nitrogen-rich diimino heterocycle, an N-F bond, a difluoromethyl-bearing ring and a cyclopentadiene ring bearing a fluoromethyl ketone. Other leaders use fluoromethyl esters, exocyclic imines, thiols and tightly fused aza rings. Carbon-fluorine and multiply fluorinated-carbon chemistry is present; it is not the missing capability. Parent leaders are also fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles, but more often retain conventional saturated amino-ring environments. Both sets remain questionable as synthesis-ready molecules because of reactive decorations and unusual topology.
liabilities: There are 381 N-halogen and 327 O-halogen-containing molecules, versus 399 and twenty in Parent. A high-listed acyl-fluoride variant and hypofluorite-containing variant further show that fluorination is not restricted to stable carbon substituents.

Forty-two of the high-score 87 contain a ring of four atoms or fewer. Multiple ring fusions, imino tautomerism and undefined configuration complicate interpretation of a single accepted graph; no stability or conformer calculation was performed.
Twenty-four molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms, and two exceed fifty. The very low scores at both tails do not support either as useful chemistry here.
missing_features: Conventional nonaromatic nonamide nitrogen environments are scarce near the Child leaders: the structural query matches two of the high-score 87 versus 52 in Parent. Exocyclic imines and heteroaromatic nitrogens dominate instead. This is an observed coverage contrast, not evidence that a particular amine is the objective's answer.

Defined stereochemistry and stable functional-group combinations are missing around the fluorinated ring/linker motifs: 74 of the high-score 87 have unassigned SP3 stereocentres, while the common N-F and O-halogen decoration is not evidence of a controlled, isolable chemical series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated diimino polycycle scores 0.5890257516535592; related leaders score 0.5659616835652702 and 0.5607574050782042. The large doubled heterocyclic construction scores 4.142021431563773e-28, and a bare fluorine record scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The high-score decile lies within 25-31 heavy atoms, consistent with a narrow useful size/composition region rather than unbounded growth or halogen count. However, 73 of those 87 contain an N-halogen bond and 24 an O-halogen bond. The N-F/imino/fluorocarbon motif is associated with higher scores in this stream; the data do not show that its reactive bonds are stable or necessary. A late amino/amide/O-Br variant scores only 0.00044210724534082373, so simply adding nitrogen or polar groups is not uniformly favorable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-06e791e9d199, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 4350 accepted optimizer molecules excluding initial records: 1003 have N-halogen bonds and 688 have O-halogen bonds; the same definitions give 888 and 162 for actual Parent n-cf8d309c06de. These motifs also occur in high-score families, including an aminooxy/N-chloro/O-Br leader. Yet 260 Child molecules already contain multiply halogenated carbon, so lack of carbon-polyhalogen capability is not the observed gap. Definitions, actual paths and hashes are preserved in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry separate from ordinary carbon-halogen substitution.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A broader chemically usable construction vocabulary would distinguish the attachment environment and reactivity of a halogen bond while retaining access to stable carbon substituents. This describes missing chemical discrimination, not a new score, a mandatory filter, or evidence that removing every flagged group improves optimization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-06e791e9d199 under the same complete Search panel and accepted-output scope: 2018 molecules contain at least one RDKit-perceived unassigned SP3 stereocentre, with 4464 such centres in total; specified tetrahedral and double-bond stereo are both absent. There are 1233 small-ring-containing molecules and 111 with a small ring made entirely of aromatic atoms. The cited bridged amine leader itself has six unassigned SP3 centres. Non-SP3 perception hits are explicitly excluded from the stereo counts. All definitions and input hashes are in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic and highly constrained ring graphs without expressing their configuration or establishing geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration-aware graph construction and geometry-aware handling of fusion, bridging and contraction are missing output capabilities. They must preserve legitimate small rings and distinguish graph flags from demonstrated physical infeasibility. These observations establish neither a stereoisomer score preference nor the feasibility of any specific cage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-06e791e9d199, Search seeds 0/1/2, excluding initial observations: 99 of 4350 molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms, 126 have fewer than twelve and 194 have more than fifty; the actual Parent counts are 91, 124 and 44 under identical strict inequalities. Atomic/diatomic fragments and large duplicated heterocyclic graphs occur among the cited low-score examples, while the Child high-score decile on every objective has no molecule above fifty. Provenance and the separate tails are retained in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular scale while changing connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic construction needs the ability to vary a connected core while retaining coherent molecular context and avoiding repeated loss or duplication of most of it. These output distributions do not identify the responsible operator or justify a universal minimum/maximum size rule; they describe the chemistry that is not being maintained.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-06e791e9d199, complete Search panel: 1501 nonempty typed and 941 generic Murcko identities occur across 4350 optimizer outputs, but the per-objective high-score groups of 87 occupy only 10, 9, 29, 23 and 18 typed scaffolds in the frozen objective order. A cited amide series differing by chloromethyl, fluoromethyl or bromomethyl has the same observed score 0.47189631731668286. These are accepted-stream associations, not evidence about unobserved populations or component causation; see policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-score chemistry repeatedly narrows to close scaffold families despite broad full-stream connectivity variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is reliable access to chemically distinct core/linker arrangements that preserve useful local functional relationships. More Murcko identities or substituent permutations alone do not demonstrate that capability, and this observation supplies no basis for imposing a diversity reward or claiming a particular construction activated.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-06e791e9d199 and actual Parent n-cf8d309c06de under identical Search seeds and 4350-optimizer-output scope: Child has nine nitrile-containing molecules versus 260 for Parent. Conventional nonaromatic nonamide nitrogen is abundant in one high-score family but scarce in another, where imino and N-halogen heterocycles dominate. Formal charge is present in 230 Child molecules, overwhelmingly as unusual charged aza-aromatic decorations; it is not absent, and no pKa was measured. SMARTS, counts and origins are in policy/scratch/r0071-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable polar and ionizable functional-group coverage is uneven despite extensive heteroatom editing.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need repeatable access to ordinary stable donor, acceptor and amino-group arrangements across evolving scaffolds, with explicit chemically meaningful charge states. This is a coverage limitation, not proof that any group is impossible to construct, that inheritance is its only source, or that adding one improves an objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
